51: - **Continuation**: Let `rustfmt` determine continuation indentation
52: 
53: ### Braces
54: 
55: Use standard Rust brace placement:
56: 
57: ```rust
58: if condition {
59:     run_primary();
60: } else {
61:     run_fallback();
62: }
63: 
64: fn run_primary() {}
65: 
66: fn run_fallback() {}
67: ```
68: 
69: ### Semicolons
70: 
71: Use semicolons for statements and omit the semicolon from an expression intentionally returned from a block.
72: 
73: ```rust
74: fn doubled(value: u32) -> u32 {
75:     value * 2
76: }
77: 
78: fn record(value: u32, output: &mut Vec<u32>) {
79:     output.push(value);
80: }
81: ```
82: 
83: Do not add `return` solely to avoid understanding a short tail expression. Use explicit `return` for early exits.
84: 
85: ```rust
86: fn normalize(value: f64) -> Result<f64, &'static str> {
87:     if !value.is_finite() {
88:         return Err("value must be finite");
89:     }
90: 
91:     Ok(value)
92: }
93: ```
94: 
95: ### Line Length
96: 
97: - Follow the workspace `rustfmt` configuration.
98: - Prefer source that remains readable near 100 characters.
99: - Allow formatter-controlled exceptions for URLs, generated names, and signatures that become less readable when manually decomposed.
100: - Do not use `#[rustfmt::skip]` for ordinary handwritten code.
101: 
102: ### Trailing Commas
103: 
104: Use trailing commas in multiline structs, enums, calls, arrays, tuples, and parameter lists.
105: 
106: ```rust
107: struct SearchConfig {
108:     query: String,
109:     limit: u32,
110:     include_metadata: bool,
111: }
112: 
113: fn search(
114:     config: &SearchConfig,
115:     candidates: &[Candidate],
116: ) -> Result<Vec<Candidate>, SearchError> {
117:     Ok(candidates.to_vec())
118: }
119: 
120: #[derive(Clone)]
121: struct Candidate;
122: 
123: #[derive(Debug)]
124: struct SearchError;
125: ```
126: 
127: ### Multiline Types
128: 
129: Break complex types at logical boundaries. Introduce a descriptive type alias when it clarifies a domain concept rather than merely shortening a line.
130: 
131: ```rust
132: use std::collections::BTreeMap;
133: 
134: type RankedByGroup = BTreeMap<String, Vec<RankedCandidate>>;
135: 
136: #[derive(Debug)]
137: struct RankedCandidate {
138:     id: String,
139:     score: f64,
140: }
141: 
142: fn group_ranked_candidates(
143:     candidates: impl IntoIterator<Item = RankedCandidate>,
144: ) -> RankedByGroup {
145:     let mut grouped = BTreeMap::new();
146: 
147:     for candidate in candidates {
148:         grouped
149:             .entry(candidate.id.clone())
150:             .or_insert_with(Vec::new)
151:             .push(candidate);
152:     }
153: 
154:     grouped
155: }
156: ```
157: 
158: ### Match Formatting
159: 
160: Prefer exhaustive `match` expressions for boundary-relevant enums and errors.
161: 
162: ```rust
163: enum CoreError {
164:     InvalidInput,
165:     NonFiniteScore,
166:     InternalInvariant,
167: }
168: 
169: fn error_code(error: &CoreError) -> &'static str {
170:     match error {
171:         CoreError::InvalidInput => "INVALID_INPUT",
172:         CoreError::NonFiniteScore => "NON_FINITE_SCORE",
173:         CoreError::InternalInvariant => "INTERNAL_INVARIANT",
174:     }
175: }
176: ```
177: 
178: Do not add a wildcard arm merely to silence a new variant in an adapter. Exhaustive matching protects JavaScript error-code parity.
179: 
180: ### Numeric Literals
181: 
182: Use separators when they clarify scale:
183: 
184: ```rust
185: const MICROS_PER_UNIT: f64 = 1_000_000.0;
186: const MAX_SAFE_INTEGER: u64 = 9_007_199_254_740_991;
187: ```
188: 
189: Do not use magic constants for parity-sensitive operations. Name the scale, radix, delimiter, truncation length, and algorithm parameters.
190: 
191: ### Deterministic Collection Formatting
192: 
193: Use canonical collection types when order is observable:
194: 
195: ```rust
196: use std::collections::BTreeMap;
197: 
198: fn canonical_metadata() -> BTreeMap<String, String> {
199:     BTreeMap::from([
200:         ("kind".to_owned(), "memory".to_owned()),
201:         ("state".to_owned(), "active".to_owned()),
202:     ])
203: }
204: ```
205: 
206: Do not rely on `HashMap` or `HashSet` iteration for:
207: 
208: - Serialized output
209: - Hash preimages
210: - Deterministic identifiers
211: - Ranking or traversal
212: - Snapshot text
213: - JavaScript-visible arrays
214: - Diagnostic output covered by golden fixtures
215: 
216: ### Sorting Rules
217: 
218: Every observable sort MUST use a complete comparator with a deterministic unique terminal key.
219: 
220: ```rust
221: use std::cmp::Ordering;
222: 
223: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
224: struct RankedCandidate {
225:     id: String,
226:     score: f64,
227:     source_index: u32,
228: }
229: 
230: fn sort_candidates(candidates: &mut [RankedCandidate]) {
231:     candidates.sort_by(|left, right| {
232:         right
233:             .score
234:             .total_cmp(&left.score)
235:             .then_with(|| left.id.cmp(&right.id))
236:             .then_with(|| left.source_index.cmp(&right.source_index))
237:     });
238: }
239: ```
240: 
241: Requirements:
242: 
243: - Reject non-finite values before sorting unless their order is explicitly contracted.
244: - Do not use `partial_cmp(...).unwrap()`.
245: - Do not use `sort_unstable*` for parity-visible output.
246: - Do not treat stable input order as the terminal tie-break.
247: - Verify lexical ordering against the permitted TypeScript identifier alphabet.
248: - Do not assume Rust `str::cmp` is equivalent to locale-sensitive JavaScript comparison.
249: 
250: ### Numeric Parity Helpers
251: 
252: Keep distinct TypeScript operations in distinct helpers.
253: 
254: ```rust
255: const SIX_DECIMAL_SCALE: f64 = 1_000_000.0;
256: 
257: fn round_scaled_six(value: f64) -> Result<f64, &'static str> {
258:     if !value.is_finite() {
259:         return Err("value must be finite");
260:     }
261: 
262:     let rounded = (value * SIX_DECIMAL_SCALE).round() / SIX_DECIMAL_SCALE;
263:     Ok(if rounded == 0.0 { 0.0 } else { rounded })
264: }
265: 
266: fn fixed_six_text(value: f64) -> Result<String, &'static str> {
267:     if !value.is_finite() {
268:         return Err("value must be finite");
269:     }
270: 
271:     Ok(format!("{value:.6}"))
272: }
273: ```
274: 
275: These helpers demonstrate separate operations; they do not establish TypeScript equivalence by themselves. JavaScript and Rust differ on rounding edge cases, negative zero, and number spelling. Each parity helper requires exhaustive fixtures generated by the pinned TypeScript oracle.
276: 
277: Never substitute one of the following without fixture evidence:
278: 
279: - `format!("{value:.6}")`
280: - `f64::to_string`
281: - A shortest-round-trip formatter
282: - `serde_json` number serialization
283: - `(value * scale).round() / scale`
284: 
285: ---
286: 
287: ## 3. IMPORT AND MODULE ORDERING
288: 
289: ### Import Group Order
290: 
291: Rust imports follow a three-group ordering with blank lines between groups:
292: 
293: ```rust
294: // 1. Standard library
295: use std::cmp::Ordering;
296: use std::collections::BTreeMap;
297: 
298: // 2. Third-party crates
299: use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
300: use thiserror::Error;
301: 
302: // 3. Current crate
303: use crate::error::CoreError;
304: use crate::ids::SymbolId;
305: ```
306: 
307: Within each group:
308: 
309: - Let `rustfmt` normalize brace layout.
310: - Sort imports lexically.
311: - Prefer one import tree per root where it remains readable.
312: - Do not use wildcard imports outside tightly scoped test preludes or established macro preludes.
313: - Keep trait imports visible when they enable methods whose origin would otherwise be unclear.
314: 
315: ### `self`, `super`, and `crate`
316: 
317: Use absolute `crate::` paths for ordinary cross-module imports. Use `super::` for parent-relative test or implementation details when the relationship is local and stable.
318: 
319: ```rust
320: use crate::error::CoreError;
321: use crate::ranking::RankedCandidate;
322: ```
323: 
324: Unit tests commonly import the module under test through `super`:
325: 
326: ```rust
327: #[cfg(test)]
328: mod tests {
329:     use super::{round_scaled_six, SIX_DECIMAL_SCALE};
330: 
331:     #[test]
332:     fn scale_is_six_decimal_places() {
333:         assert_eq!(SIX_DECIMAL_SCALE, 1_000_000.0);
334:         assert_eq!(round_scaled_six(1.0), Ok(1.0));
335:     }
336: }
337: ```
338: 
339: ### Module Declaration Order
340: 
341: Place module declarations after imports and before ordinary types or functions unless the crate root uses declarations as its primary index.
342: 
343: ```rust
344: mod dto;
345: mod error;
346: mod ids;
347: mod ranking;
348: 
349: pub use dto::{SearchOptions, SearchResult};
350: pub use error::CoreError;
351: pub use ids::SymbolId;
352: pub use ranking::rank_candidates;
353: ```
354: 
355: ### Re-Exports
356: 
357: Re-export only the intended stable surface.
358: 
359: ```rust
360: mod error;
361: mod ranking;
362: 
363: pub use error::CoreError;
364: pub use ranking::{rank_candidates, Candidate, RankedCandidate};
365: ```
366: 
367: Avoid:
368: 
369: ```rust
370: pub use ranking::*;
371: ```
372: 
373: Broad re-exports make accidental API growth difficult to detect and can expose adapter-internal types.
374: 
375: ### Macro Imports
376: 
377: Import derive macros and attributes explicitly:
378: 
379: ```rust
380: use napi_derive::napi;
381: use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
382: use thiserror::Error;
383: ```
384: 
385: Do not use `#[macro_use] extern crate ...` in modern Rust.
386: 
387: ### Conditional Imports
388: 
389: Keep target-specific imports close to the target-specific module. Prefer separate adapter crates. When conditional compilation is necessary, make it explicit:
390: 
391: ```rust
392: #[cfg(feature = "native")]
393: use napi::bindgen_prelude::Buffer;
394: 
395: #[cfg(feature = "wasm")]
396: use wasm_bindgen::prelude::JsValue;
397: ```
398: 
399: Do not conditionally import runtime values into the pure core.
400: 
401: ### Dependency Direction
402: 
403: The permitted dependency direction is:
404: 
405: ```text
406: napi adapter ─┐
407: wasm adapter ─┼──> pure core
408: sidecar ──────┘
409: ```
410: 
411: The pure core MUST NOT depend on:
412: 
413: - `napi`
414: - `napi-derive`
415: - `wasm-bindgen`
416: - `JsValue`
417: - Node handles
418: - WASM runtime handles
419: - Sidecar framing or process I/O
420: 
421: This protects the transport-neutral core contract and prevents runtime-specific behavior from changing deterministic algorithms.
422: 
423: ---

12: 
13: # Rust/TypeScript Interop — Errors, Parity & Related Resources
14: 
15: Formatting standards, naming conventions, and TypeScript interoperability rules for Rust files in the OpenCode development environment.
16: 
17: ---
18: 
19: ## 1. OVERVIEW
20: 
21: ### Purpose
22: 
23: Shows how a Rust boundary reports errors, serializes results and exposes itself through napi-rs or wasm-bindgen without breaking TypeScript parity.
24: 
25: ### When to Use
26: 
27: - Defining a core error type or its JavaScript mapping
28: - Removing a panic path from boundary validation
29: - Building deterministic identifiers or stable serialization
30: - Writing a napi-rs or wasm-bindgen export
31: - Wiring a fallback or a differential parity test
32: 
33: ---
34: 
35: ## 2. ERROR STYLE
36: 
37: Core public operations return domain-specific `Result` values backed by `thiserror`.
38: 
39: ```rust
40: use thiserror::Error;
41: 
42: #[derive(Debug, Error)]
43: pub enum RankingError {
44:     #[error("candidate identifier must not be empty")]
45:     EmptyIdentifier,
46: 
47:     #[error("candidate score must be finite")]
48:     NonFiniteScore,
49: 
50:     #[error("candidate limit {limit} exceeds maximum {maximum}")]
51:     LimitExceeded {
52:         limit: u32,
53:         maximum: u32,
54:     },
55: }
56: ```
57: 
58: Rules:
59: 
60: - Core errors contain adapter-relevant structured context.
61: - Core errors contain no napi-rs, WASM, or Node runtime types.
62: - `anyhow` is prohibited in pure-core public APIs and exported functions.
63: - `anyhow` MAY be used in sidecar `main`, build tooling, and the outermost non-ABI shell.
64: - Every adapter owns one exhaustive mapping from core errors to stable JavaScript errors.
65: - Error messages and codes covered by TypeScript contracts are golden-tested.
66: - Panic only for an impossible internal invariant, never for recoverable boundary input.
67: 
68: ---
69: 
70: ## 3. EXHAUSTIVE ADAPTER ERROR MAPPING
71: 
72: ```rust
73: #[derive(Debug)]
74: struct JsErrorShape {
75:     code: &'static str,
76:     message: String,
77: }
78: 
79: fn map_ranking_error(error: RankingError) -> JsErrorShape {
80:     match error {
81:         RankingError::EmptyIdentifier => JsErrorShape {
82:             code: "INVALID_IDENTIFIER",
83:             message: error.to_string(),
84:         },
85:         RankingError::NonFiniteScore => JsErrorShape {
86:             code: "NON_FINITE_SCORE",
87:             message: error.to_string(),
88:         },
89:         RankingError::LimitExceeded { .. } => JsErrorShape {
90:             code: "LIMIT_EXCEEDED",
91:             message: error.to_string(),
92:         },
93:     }
94: }
95: ```
96: 
97: The adapter must also preserve whether the existing TypeScript operation throws synchronously or rejects a Promise.
98: 
99: ---
100: 
101: ## 4. PANIC-FREE BOUNDARY VALIDATION
102: 
103: Do not use:
104: 
105: ```rust
106: let score = input.parse::<f64>().unwrap();
107: let first = candidates[0].clone();
108: let ordering = left.score.partial_cmp(&right.score).unwrap();
109: ```
110: 
111: Use typed failures:
112: 
113: ```rust
114: use std::num::ParseFloatError;
115: 
116: fn parse_score(input: &str) -> Result<f64, ParseFloatError> {
117:     input.parse::<f64>()
118: }
119: 
120: fn first_candidate(candidates: &[String]) -> Option<&str> {
121:     candidates.first().map(String::as_str)
122: }
123: ```
124: 
125: JavaScript-controlled data must not reach:
126: 
127: - `unwrap`
128: - `expect`
129: - Unchecked indexing
130: - `panic!`
131: - `unreachable!`
132: - Assertions used as validation
133: - `partial_cmp(...).unwrap()`
134: 
135: ---
136: 
137: ## 5. DETERMINISTIC IDENTIFIERS
138: 
139: Identifier generation preserves the exact TypeScript preimage contract:
140: 
141: - Input fields
142: - Field order
143: - Separators
144: - UTF-8 encoding
145: - Hash algorithm
146: - Lowercase hexadecimal encoding
147: - Truncation length
148: 
149: ```rust
150: use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};
151: 
152: fn deterministic_id(namespace: &str, name: &str) -> String {
153:     let preimage = format!("{namespace}\0{name}");
154:     let digest = Sha256::digest(preimage.as_bytes());
155:     let hexadecimal = format!("{digest:x}");
156:     hexadecimal[..24].to_owned()
157: }
158: ```
159: 
160: This example is correct only if the TypeScript oracle uses the same fields, NUL delimiter, UTF-8 bytes, SHA-256, lowercase hexadecimal output, and 24-character truncation. Never infer those details from a semantically similar implementation.
161: 
162: ---
163: 
164: ## 6. STABLE SERIALIZATION
165: 
166: Do not assume `serde_json` reproduces JavaScript byte output automatically.
167: 
168: Potential differences include:
169: 
170: - Number spelling
171: - Negative zero
172: - Exponent notation
173: - Omitted versus `null` fields
174: - Escaping
175: - Key order
176: - Non-finite values
177: - Map iteration order
178: 
179: Use passive DTOs and canonical maps:
180: 
181: ```rust
182: use std::collections::BTreeMap;
183: 
184: use serde::Serialize;
185: 
186: #[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
187: #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
188: struct SearchResponse {
189:     results: Vec<SearchResult>,
190:     metadata: BTreeMap<String, String>,
191: }
192: 
193: #[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
194: struct SearchResult {
195:     id: String,
196:     score: f64,
197: }
198: ```
199: 
200: Byte-for-byte fixtures remain required even when the Rust structure appears equivalent to the TypeScript object.
201: 
202: ---
203: 
204: ## 7. ASYNC AND THREADING
205: 
206: Keep parsing, scoring, ranking, hashing, canonicalization, and serialization preparation synchronous in the core.
207: 
208: Use napi-rs `AsyncTask` only for measured CPU or blocking work that would materially block Node.
209: 
210: Before worker execution:
211: 
212: - Convert JavaScript values into owned DTOs.
213: - Copy JavaScript-owned buffers.
214: - Validate cheap structural constraints.
215: - Do not retain `Env`, `JsValue`, or thread-affine handles.
216: 
217: After worker execution:
218: 
219: - Reorder results by deterministic sequence keys.
220: - Canonicalize output synchronously.
221: - Map typed errors on the JavaScript thread.
222: 
223: Use Tokio only for genuine Rust-owned asynchronous I/O. Use Rayon only after benchmark evidence demonstrates a useful batch-size threshold.
224: 
225: Parity-visible floating-point reductions MUST NOT run in nondeterministic parallel order. If parallel reduction is unavoidable, fix the reduction tree and golden-test it across every supported target.
226: 
227: Baseline WASM is single-threaded. Promise bridging does not create CPU parallelism.
228: 
229: ---
230: 
231: ## 8. NAPI-RS EXPORT EXAMPLE
232: 
233: ```rust
234: use napi::bindgen_prelude::{Error, Status};
235: use napi_derive::napi;
236: 
237: #[napi(object)]
238: pub struct CandidateDto {
239:     pub id: String,
240:     pub score: f64,
241: }
242: 
243: #[napi(js_name = "rankCandidates")]
244: pub fn rank_candidates(candidates: Vec<CandidateDto>) -> napi::Result<Vec<CandidateDto>> {
245:     let mut candidates = candidates;
246: 
247:     if candidates.iter().any(|candidate| !candidate.score.is_finite()) {
248:         return Err(Error::new(
249:             Status::InvalidArg,
250:             "NON_FINITE_SCORE: candidate score must be finite",
251:         ));
252:     }
253: 
254:     candidates.sort_by(|left, right| {
255:         right
256:             .score
257:             .total_cmp(&left.score)
258:             .then_with(|| left.id.cmp(&right.id))
259:     });
260: 
261:     Ok(candidates)
262: }
263: ```
264: 
265: In production, ranking belongs in the pure core and the adapter converts DTOs and errors only. The example shows the JavaScript-visible naming and owned boundary shape.
266: 
267: ---
268: 
269: ## 9. WASM-BINDGEN EXPORT EXAMPLE
270: 
271: ```rust
272: use wasm_bindgen::prelude::*;
273: 
274: #[wasm_bindgen(js_name = normalizeScore)]
275: pub fn normalize_score(value: f64) -> Result<f64, JsValue> {
276:     if !value.is_finite() {
277:         return Err(JsValue::from_str(
278:             "NON_FINITE_SCORE: score must be finite",
279:         ));
280:     }
281: 
282:     let normalized = (value * 1_000_000.0).round() / 1_000_000.0;
283:     Ok(if normalized == 0.0 { 0.0 } else { normalized })
284: }
285: ```
286: 
287: The exact rounding implementation and error shape require differential fixtures against the TypeScript oracle before release.
288: 
289: ---
290: 
291: ## 10. COEXISTENCE AND FALLBACKS
292: 
293: TypeScript retains fallback selection. Rust adapters expose capability; they do not silently choose themselves.
294: 
295: ```typescript
296: const result = flags.nativeRanking && nativeAddon !== null
297:   ? await nativeAddon.rankCandidates(input)
298:   : await rankCandidatesTypeScript(input);
299: ```
300: 
301: Both paths must emit identical bytes for the supported input domain. A semantic deep-equality test is useful for diagnosis but does not replace the byte comparison.
302: 
303: ---
304: 
305: ## 11. DIFFERENTIAL TEST CONTRACT
306: 
307: The release-level assertion is:
308: 
309: ```rust
310: fn assert_byte_parity(
311:     typescript_bytes: &[u8],
312:     rust_bytes: &[u8],
313: ) {
314:     assert_eq!(typescript_bytes, rust_bytes);
315: }
316: ```
317: 
318: Golden fixtures MUST originate from the pinned TypeScript oracle. Rust must not author or automatically accept its own expected output.
319: 
320: Parity fixtures cover:
321: 
322: - Six-decimal edge cases
323: - Positive and negative halfway values
324: - Negative zero
325: - Very small and very large finite numbers
326: - Complete sorting ties
327: - Identifier alphabet boundaries
328: - Unicode and UTF-8 preimages
329: - Optional and omitted fields
330: - Empty collections
331: - Map and object ordering
332: - Error codes and exact messages
333: - Synchronous throws and Promise rejections
334: - Native and WASM artifacts
335: 
336: ---
337: 
338: ## 12. RELATED RESOURCES
339: 
340: - [quality-standards.md](../quality-standards/overview-and-data-ownership.md) - Ownership, safety, ABI contracts, error translation, concurrency, Cargo, and parity gates
341: - [quick-reference.md](../quick-reference/overview-and-boundary-template.md) - Copy-paste Rust boundary templates, deterministic recipes, and build commands

53:         maximum: u32,
54:     },
55: }
56: ```
57: 
58: Rules:
59: 
60: - Core errors contain adapter-relevant structured context.
61: - Core errors contain no napi-rs, WASM, or Node runtime types.
62: - `anyhow` is prohibited in pure-core public APIs and exported functions.
63: - `anyhow` MAY be used in sidecar `main`, build tooling, and the outermost non-ABI shell.
64: - Every adapter owns one exhaustive mapping from core errors to stable JavaScript errors.
65: - Error messages and codes covered by TypeScript contracts are golden-tested.
66: - Panic only for an impossible internal invariant, never for recoverable boundary input.
67: 
68: ---
69: 
70: ## 3. EXHAUSTIVE ADAPTER ERROR MAPPING
71: 
72: ```rust
73: #[derive(Debug)]
74: struct JsErrorShape {
75:     code: &'static str,
76:     message: String,
77: }
78: 
79: fn map_ranking_error(error: RankingError) -> JsErrorShape {
80:     match error {
81:         RankingError::EmptyIdentifier => JsErrorShape {
82:             code: "INVALID_IDENTIFIER",
83:             message: error.to_string(),
84:         },
85:         RankingError::NonFiniteScore => JsErrorShape {
86:             code: "NON_FINITE_SCORE",
87:             message: error.to_string(),
88:         },
89:         RankingError::LimitExceeded { .. } => JsErrorShape {
90:             code: "LIMIT_EXCEEDED",
91:             message: error.to_string(),
92:         },
93:     }
94: }
95: ```
96: 
97: The adapter must also preserve whether the existing TypeScript operation throws synchronously or rejects a Promise.
98: 
99: ---
100: 
101: ## 4. PANIC-FREE BOUNDARY VALIDATION
102: 
103: Do not use:
104: 
105: ```rust
106: let score = input.parse::<f64>().unwrap();
107: let first = candidates[0].clone();
108: let ordering = left.score.partial_cmp(&right.score).unwrap();
109: ```
110: 
111: Use typed failures:
112: 
113: ```rust
114: use std::num::ParseFloatError;
115: 
116: fn parse_score(input: &str) -> Result<f64, ParseFloatError> {
117:     input.parse::<f64>()
118: }
119: 
120: fn first_candidate(candidates: &[String]) -> Option<&str> {
121:     candidates.first().map(String::as_str)
122: }
123: ```
124: 
125: JavaScript-controlled data must not reach:
126: 
127: - `unwrap`
128: - `expect`
129: - Unchecked indexing
130: - `panic!`
131: - `unreachable!`
132: - Assertions used as validation
133: - `partial_cmp(...).unwrap()`
134: 
135: ---
136: 
137: ## 5. DETERMINISTIC IDENTIFIERS
138: 
139: Identifier generation preserves the exact TypeScript preimage contract:
140: 
141: - Input fields
142: - Field order
143: - Separators
144: - UTF-8 encoding
145: - Hash algorithm
146: - Lowercase hexadecimal encoding
147: - Truncation length
148: 
149: ```rust
150: use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};
151: 
152: fn deterministic_id(namespace: &str, name: &str) -> String {
153:     let preimage = format!("{namespace}\0{name}");
154:     let digest = Sha256::digest(preimage.as_bytes());
155:     let hexadecimal = format!("{digest:x}");
156:     hexadecimal[..24].to_owned()
157: }
158: ```
159: 
160: This example is correct only if the TypeScript oracle uses the same fields, NUL delimiter, UTF-8 bytes, SHA-256, lowercase hexadecimal output, and 24-character truncation. Never infer those details from a semantically similar implementation.
161: 
162: ---
163: 
164: ## 6. STABLE SERIALIZATION
165: 
166: Do not assume `serde_json` reproduces JavaScript byte output automatically.
167: 
168: Potential differences include:
169: 
170: - Number spelling
171: - Negative zero
172: - Exponent notation
173: - Omitted versus `null` fields
174: - Escaping
175: - Key order
176: - Non-finite values
177: - Map iteration order
178: 
179: Use passive DTOs and canonical maps:
180: 
181: ```rust
182: use std::collections::BTreeMap;
183: 
184: use serde::Serialize;
185: 
186: #[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
187: #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
188: struct SearchResponse {
189:     results: Vec<SearchResult>,
190:     metadata: BTreeMap<String, String>,
191: }
192: 
193: #[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
194: struct SearchResult {
195:     id: String,
196:     score: f64,
197: }
198: ```
199: 
200: Byte-for-byte fixtures remain required even when the Rust structure appears equivalent to the TypeScript object.
201: 
202: ---
203: 
204: ## 7. ASYNC AND THREADING
205: 
206: Keep parsing, scoring, ranking, hashing, canonicalization, and serialization preparation synchronous in the core.
207: 
208: Use napi-rs `AsyncTask` only for measured CPU or blocking work that would materially block Node.
209: 
210: Before worker execution:
211: 
212: - Convert JavaScript values into owned DTOs.
213: - Copy JavaScript-owned buffers.
214: - Validate cheap structural constraints.
215: - Do not retain `Env`, `JsValue`, or thread-affine handles.
216: 
217: After worker execution:
218: 
219: - Reorder results by deterministic sequence keys.
220: - Canonicalize output synchronously.
221: - Map typed errors on the JavaScript thread.
222: 
223: Use Tokio only for genuine Rust-owned asynchronous I/O. Use Rayon only after benchmark evidence demonstrates a useful batch-size threshold.
224: 
225: Parity-visible floating-point reductions MUST NOT run in nondeterministic parallel order. If parallel reduction is unavoidable, fix the reduction tree and golden-test it across every supported target.
226: 
227: Baseline WASM is single-threaded. Promise bridging does not create CPU parallelism.
228: 
229: ---
230: 
231: ## 8. NAPI-RS EXPORT EXAMPLE
232: 
233: ```rust
234: use napi::bindgen_prelude::{Error, Status};
235: use napi_derive::napi;
236: 
237: #[napi(object)]
238: pub struct CandidateDto {
239:     pub id: String,
240:     pub score: f64,
241: }
242: 
243: #[napi(js_name = "rankCandidates")]
244: pub fn rank_candidates(candidates: Vec<CandidateDto>) -> napi::Result<Vec<CandidateDto>> {
245:     let mut candidates = candidates;
246: 
247:     if candidates.iter().any(|candidate| !candidate.score.is_finite()) {
248:         return Err(Error::new(
249:             Status::InvalidArg,
250:             "NON_FINITE_SCORE: candidate score must be finite",
251:         ));
252:     }
253: 
254:     candidates.sort_by(|left, right| {
255:         right
256:             .score
257:             .total_cmp(&left.score)
258:             .then_with(|| left.id.cmp(&right.id))
259:     });
260: 
261:     Ok(candidates)
262: }
263: ```
264: 
265: In production, ranking belongs in the pure core and the adapter converts DTOs and errors only. The example shows the JavaScript-visible naming and owned boundary shape.
266: 
267: ---
268: 
269: ## 9. WASM-BINDGEN EXPORT EXAMPLE
270: 
271: ```rust
272: use wasm_bindgen::prelude::*;
273: 
274: #[wasm_bindgen(js_name = normalizeScore)]
275: pub fn normalize_score(value: f64) -> Result<f64, JsValue> {
276:     if !value.is_finite() {
277:         return Err(JsValue::from_str(
278:             "NON_FINITE_SCORE: score must be finite",
279:         ));
280:     }
281: 
282:     let normalized = (value * 1_000_000.0).round() / 1_000_000.0;
283:     Ok(if normalized == 0.0 { 0.0 } else { normalized })
284: }
285: ```
286: 
287: The exact rounding implementation and error shape require differential fixtures against the TypeScript oracle before release.
288: 
289: ---
290: 
291: ## 10. COEXISTENCE AND FALLBACKS
292: 
293: TypeScript retains fallback selection. Rust adapters expose capability; they do not silently choose themselves.
294: 
295: ```typescript
296: const result = flags.nativeRanking && nativeAddon !== null
297:   ? await nativeAddon.rankCandidates(input)
298:   : await rankCandidatesTypeScript(input);
299: ```
300: 
301: Both paths must emit identical bytes for the supported input domain. A semantic deep-equality test is useful for diagnosis but does not replace the byte comparison.
302: 
303: ---
304: 
305: ## 11. DIFFERENTIAL TEST CONTRACT
306: 
307: The release-level assertion is:
308: 
309: ```rust
310: fn assert_byte_parity(
311:     typescript_bytes: &[u8],
312:     rust_bytes: &[u8],
313: ) {
314:     assert_eq!(typescript_bytes, rust_bytes);
315: }
316: ```
317: 
318: Golden fixtures MUST originate from the pinned TypeScript oracle. Rust must not author or automatically accept its own expected output.
319: 
320: Parity fixtures cover:
321: 
322: - Six-decimal edge cases
323: - Positive and negative halfway values
324: - Negative zero
325: - Very small and very large finite numbers
326: - Complete sorting ties
327: - Identifier alphabet boundaries
328: - Unicode and UTF-8 preimages
329: - Optional and omitted fields
330: - Empty collections
331: - Map and object ordering
332: - Error codes and exact messages
333: - Synchronous throws and Promise rejections
334: - Native and WASM artifacts
335: 
336: ---
337: 
338: ## 12. RELATED RESOURCES
339: 
340: - [quality-standards.md](../quality-standards/overview-and-data-ownership.md) - Ownership, safety, ABI contracts, error translation, concurrency, Cargo, and parity gates
341: - [quick-reference.md](../quick-reference/overview-and-boundary-template.md) - Copy-paste Rust boundary templates, deterministic recipes, and build commands

13: # Rust/TypeScript Interop — Model & Boundary Types
14: 
15: Formatting standards, naming conventions, and TypeScript interoperability rules for Rust files in the OpenCode development environment.
16: 
17: ---
18: 
19: ## 1. OVERVIEW
20: 
21: ### Purpose
22: 
23: Draws the line between TypeScript ownership and Rust compute, then fixes the boundary type, buffer and enumeration shapes that cross it.
24: 
25: ### When to Use
26: 
27: - Deciding whether logic belongs in TypeScript, the pure core or a thin adapter
28: - Designing an owned or borrowed boundary type
29: - Handling buffer ownership or fixed-width integers
30: - Validating a DTO or implementing `From` or `TryFrom`
31: - Choosing an enum representation for JavaScript
32: 
33: ---
34: 
35: ## 2. RUST/TYPESCRIPT INTEROP AND COEXISTENCE
36: 
37: Rust supplements the existing TypeScript/Node backend. It does not replace transport ownership or redefine public MCP behavior.
38: 
39: ### Responsibility Split
40: 
41: | TypeScript/Node Owns | Rust Owns |
42: |----------------------|-----------|
43: | MCP transport and tool schemas | Measured compute kernels |
44: | Daemon and CLI wiring | Validation internal to a kernel |
45: | Feature flags and fallback selection | Deterministic ranking and hashing |
46: | Public request routing | Canonical numeric operations |
47: | Compatibility orchestration | Transport-neutral domain types |
48: | JavaScript fallback behavior | Narrow napi-rs/WASM/sidecar adapters |
49: 
50: Move code into Rust only when measurement justifies the added boundary and build complexity.
51: 
52: ### Pure Core and Thin Adapters
53: 
54: The core API accepts transport-neutral, owned inputs and returns transport-neutral, owned outputs.
55: 
56: ```rust
57: #![forbid(unsafe_code)]
58: 
59: use thiserror::Error;
60: 
61: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
62: pub struct Candidate {
63:     pub id: String,
64:     pub score: f64,
65: }
66: 
67: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
68: pub struct RankedCandidate {
69:     pub id: String,
70:     pub score: f64,
71: }
72: 
73: #[derive(Debug, Error)]
74: pub enum CoreError {
75:     #[error("candidate identifier must not be empty")]
76:     EmptyIdentifier,
77: 
78:     #[error("candidate score must be finite")]
79:     NonFiniteScore,
80: }
81: 
82: pub fn rank_candidates(
83:     candidates: Vec<Candidate>,
84: ) -> Result<Vec<RankedCandidate>, CoreError> {
85:     let mut ranked = candidates
86:         .into_iter()
87:         .map(|candidate| {
88:             if candidate.id.is_empty() {
89:                 return Err(CoreError::EmptyIdentifier);
90:             }
91: 
92:             if !candidate.score.is_finite() {
93:                 return Err(CoreError::NonFiniteScore);
94:             }
95: 
96:             Ok(RankedCandidate {
97:                 id: candidate.id,
98:                 score: candidate.score,
99:             })
100:         })
101:         .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?;
102: 
103:     ranked.sort_by(|left, right| {
104:         right
105:             .score
106:             .total_cmp(&left.score)
107:             .then_with(|| left.id.cmp(&right.id))
108:     });
109: 
110:     Ok(ranked)
111: }
112: ```
113: 
114: The adapter performs DTO conversion and stable error mapping, not ranking logic.
115: 
116: ### Owned Versus Borrowed Boundary Types
117: 
118: Export owned, materialized values:
119: 
120: - `String`
121: - `Vec<T>`
122: - Fixed-width integers such as `u32`, `i64`, and `u64`
123: - `f64` only with explicit finite-value and numeric-parity handling
124: - `bool`
125: - Passive boundary structs
126: - `Result<OwnedOutput, BoundaryError>`
127: 
128: Do not export:
129: 
130: - `&str`
131: - `&[T]`
132: - `Cow<'a, T>`
133: - Public lifetime parameters
134: - Iterators
135: - Internal graph references
136: - Core builders
137: - Type-state objects
138: - `usize` or `isize`
139: 
140: Borrow inside the core:
141: 
142: ```rust
143: fn canonical_identifier(namespace: &str, name: &str) -> String {
144:     format!("{namespace}:{name}")
145: }
146: ```
147: 
148: Materialize at the boundary:
149: 
150: ```rust
151: #[derive(Debug)]
152: struct IdentifierRequest {
153:     namespace: String,
154:     name: String,
155: }
156: 
157: fn handle_identifier(request: IdentifierRequest) -> String {
158:     canonical_identifier(&request.namespace, &request.name)
159: }
160: ```
161: 
162: ### Buffer Ownership
163: 
164: JavaScript-owned memory MUST be copied before asynchronous or cross-thread work unless a reviewed ownership protocol proves exclusive access for the full operation.
165: 
166: ```rust
167: fn prepare_async_input(input: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
168:     // The worker receives owned bytes because JavaScript may mutate or release
169:     // the source buffer after this synchronous boundary call returns.
170:     input.to_vec()
171: }
172: ```
173: 
174: Zero-copy napi-rs or WASM views are synchronous optimization exceptions. They require:
175: 
176: - Benchmark evidence
177: - Explicit lifetime and mutation rules
178: - Thread-affinity documentation
179: - Safety review
180: - Tests that challenge ownership assumptions
181: 
182: ### Fixed-Width Integers
183: 
184: Use fixed-width integers at every JavaScript-visible boundary.
185: 
186: ```rust
187: #[derive(Debug)]
188: struct PaginationDto {
189:     offset: u32,
190:     limit: u32,
191: }
192: ```
193: 
194: Never expose `usize` or `isize`; their width varies by target.
195: 
196: Integers outside JavaScript's safe range require an explicitly versioned representation:
197: 
198: ```rust
199: #[derive(Debug)]
200: struct LargeCounterDto {
201:     decimal_value: String,
202: }
203: ```
204: 
205: Use JavaScript `BigInt` only when both the binding technology and TypeScript contract explicitly require it.
206: 
207: ### DTO Validation
208: 
209: Boundary DTOs are passive and versioned. Convert them immediately into validated private-field core types.
210: 
211: ```rust
212: use thiserror::Error;
213: 
214: #[derive(Debug)]
215: struct SearchOptionsDto {
216:     limit: u32,
217:     minimum_score: f64,
218: }
219: 
220: #[derive(Debug)]
221: struct SearchOptions {
222:     limit: u32,
223:     minimum_score: FiniteScore,
224: }
225: 
226: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
227: struct FiniteScore(f64);
228: 
229: #[derive(Debug, Error)]
230: enum OptionsError {
231:     #[error("limit must be greater than zero")]
232:     EmptyLimit,
233: 
234:     #[error("minimum score must be finite")]
235:     NonFiniteScore,
236: }
237: 
238: impl TryFrom<SearchOptionsDto> for SearchOptions {
239:     type Error = OptionsError;
240: 
241:     fn try_from(dto: SearchOptionsDto) -> Result<Self, Self::Error> {
242:         if dto.limit == 0 {
243:             return Err(OptionsError::EmptyLimit);
244:         }
245: 
246:         if !dto.minimum_score.is_finite() {
247:             return Err(OptionsError::NonFiniteScore);
248:         }
249: 
250:         Ok(Self {
251:             limit: dto.limit,
252:             minimum_score: FiniteScore(dto.minimum_score),
253:         })
254:     }
255: }
256: ```
257: 
258: ### `From` and `TryFrom`
259: 
260: Use `From` only when conversion is:
261: 
262: - Infallible
263: - Lossless
264: - Value-preserving
265: - Unsurprising
266: 
267: ```rust
268: #[derive(Debug)]
269: struct RankedCandidate {
270:     id: String,
271:     score: f64,
272: }
273: 
274: #[derive(Debug)]
275: struct RankedCandidateDto {
276:     id: String,
277:     score: f64,
278: }
279: 
280: impl From<RankedCandidate> for RankedCandidateDto {
281:     fn from(candidate: RankedCandidate) -> Self {
282:         Self {
283:             id: candidate.id,
284:             score: candidate.score,
285:         }
286:     }
287: }
288: ```
289: 
290: Use `TryFrom` for:
291: 
292: - DTO validation
293: - Finite-number checks
294: - Integer narrowing
295: - Enum parsing
296: - Identifier normalization
297: - Any conversion that can reject or alter invalid input
298: 
299: ```rust
300: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
301: enum MemoryState {
302:     Active,
303:     Archived,
304: }
305: 
306: #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
307: struct StateParseError;
308: 
309: impl TryFrom<&str> for MemoryState {
310:     type Error = StateParseError;
311: 
312:     fn try_from(value: &str) -> Result<Self, Self::Error> {
313:         match value {
314:             "active" => Ok(Self::Active),
315:             "archived" => Ok(Self::Archived),
316:             _ => Err(StateParseError),
317:         }
318:     }
319: }
320: ```
321: 
322: Implement `From` or `TryFrom`, not `Into` or `TryInto`, directly.
323: 
324: ### Enum Representation
325: 
326: Use stable string discriminants or explicit numeric codes at the boundary. Never export incidental Rust ordinals.
327: 
328: ```rust
329: use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
330: 
331: #[derive(Debug, Deserialize, Serialize)]
332: #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
333: enum MemoryTierDto {
334:     Constitutional,
335:     Working,
336:     LongTerm,
337: }
338: ```
339: 
340: Do not use `variant as u8` as a wire contract unless every numeric code is explicit and versioned.
341: 
342: Use `#[non_exhaustive]` only when wildcard evolution is intentional. Adapter error mappings SHOULD remain exhaustive so new variants cannot silently receive the wrong JavaScript code.
343:

143: fn canonical_identifier(namespace: &str, name: &str) -> String {
144:     format!("{namespace}:{name}")
145: }
146: ```
147: 
148: Materialize at the boundary:
149: 
150: ```rust
151: #[derive(Debug)]
152: struct IdentifierRequest {
153:     namespace: String,
154:     name: String,
155: }
156: 
157: fn handle_identifier(request: IdentifierRequest) -> String {
158:     canonical_identifier(&request.namespace, &request.name)
159: }
160: ```
161: 
162: ### Buffer Ownership
163: 
164: JavaScript-owned memory MUST be copied before asynchronous or cross-thread work unless a reviewed ownership protocol proves exclusive access for the full operation.
165: 
166: ```rust
167: fn prepare_async_input(input: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
168:     // The worker receives owned bytes because JavaScript may mutate or release
169:     // the source buffer after this synchronous boundary call returns.
170:     input.to_vec()
171: }
172: ```
173: 
174: Zero-copy napi-rs or WASM views are synchronous optimization exceptions. They require:
175: 
176: - Benchmark evidence
177: - Explicit lifetime and mutation rules
178: - Thread-affinity documentation
179: - Safety review
180: - Tests that challenge ownership assumptions
181: 
182: ### Fixed-Width Integers
183: 
184: Use fixed-width integers at every JavaScript-visible boundary.
185: 
186: ```rust
187: #[derive(Debug)]
188: struct PaginationDto {
189:     offset: u32,
190:     limit: u32,
191: }
192: ```
193: 
194: Never expose `usize` or `isize`; their width varies by target.
195: 
196: Integers outside JavaScript's safe range require an explicitly versioned representation:
197: 
198: ```rust
199: #[derive(Debug)]
200: struct LargeCounterDto {
201:     decimal_value: String,
202: }
203: ```
204: 
205: Use JavaScript `BigInt` only when both the binding technology and TypeScript contract explicitly require it.
206: 
207: ### DTO Validation
208: 
209: Boundary DTOs are passive and versioned. Convert them immediately into validated private-field core types.
210: 
211: ```rust
212: use thiserror::Error;
213: 
214: #[derive(Debug)]
215: struct SearchOptionsDto {
216:     limit: u32,
217:     minimum_score: f64,
218: }
219: 
220: #[derive(Debug)]
221: struct SearchOptions {
222:     limit: u32,
223:     minimum_score: FiniteScore,
224: }
225: 
226: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
227: struct FiniteScore(f64);
228: 
229: #[derive(Debug, Error)]
230: enum OptionsError {
231:     #[error("limit must be greater than zero")]
232:     EmptyLimit,
233: 
234:     #[error("minimum score must be finite")]
235:     NonFiniteScore,
236: }
237: 
238: impl TryFrom<SearchOptionsDto> for SearchOptions {
239:     type Error = OptionsError;
240: 
241:     fn try_from(dto: SearchOptionsDto) -> Result<Self, Self::Error> {
242:         if dto.limit == 0 {
243:             return Err(OptionsError::EmptyLimit);
244:         }
245: 
246:         if !dto.minimum_score.is_finite() {
247:             return Err(OptionsError::NonFiniteScore);
248:         }
249: 
250:         Ok(Self {
251:             limit: dto.limit,
252:             minimum_score: FiniteScore(dto.minimum_score),
253:         })
254:     }
255: }
256: ```
257: 
258: ### `From` and `TryFrom`
259: 
260: Use `From` only when conversion is:
261: 
262: - Infallible
263: - Lossless
264: - Value-preserving
265: - Unsurprising
266: 
267: ```rust
268: #[derive(Debug)]
269: struct RankedCandidate {
270:     id: String,
271:     score: f64,
272: }
273: 
274: #[derive(Debug)]
275: struct RankedCandidateDto {
276:     id: String,
277:     score: f64,
278: }
279: 
280: impl From<RankedCandidate> for RankedCandidateDto {
281:     fn from(candidate: RankedCandidate) -> Self {
282:         Self {
283:             id: candidate.id,
284:             score: candidate.score,
285:         }
286:     }
287: }
288: ```
289: 
290: Use `TryFrom` for:
291: 
292: - DTO validation
293: - Finite-number checks
294: - Integer narrowing
295: - Enum parsing
296: - Identifier normalization
297: - Any conversion that can reject or alter invalid input
298: 
299: ```rust
300: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
301: enum MemoryState {
302:     Active,
303:     Archived,
304: }
305: 
306: #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
307: struct StateParseError;
308: 
309: impl TryFrom<&str> for MemoryState {
310:     type Error = StateParseError;
311: 
312:     fn try_from(value: &str) -> Result<Self, Self::Error> {
313:         match value {
314:             "active" => Ok(Self::Active),
315:             "archived" => Ok(Self::Archived),
316:             _ => Err(StateParseError),
317:         }
318:     }
319: }
320: ```
321: 
322: Implement `From` or `TryFrom`, not `Into` or `TryInto`, directly.
323: 
324: ### Enum Representation
325: 
326: Use stable string discriminants or explicit numeric codes at the boundary. Never export incidental Rust ordinals.
327: 
328: ```rust
329: use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
330: 
331: #[derive(Debug, Deserialize, Serialize)]
332: #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
333: enum MemoryTierDto {
334:     Constitutional,
335:     Working,
336:     LongTerm,
337: }
338: ```
339: 
340: Do not use `variant as u8` as a wire contract unless every numeric code is explicit and versioned.
341: 
342: Use `#[non_exhaustive]` only when wildcard evolution is intentional. Adapter error mappings SHOULD remain exhaustive so new variants cannot silently receive the wrong JavaScript code.

14: # Rust Style Guide
15: 
16: Formatting standards, naming conventions, and TypeScript interoperability rules for Rust files in the OpenCode development environment.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Purpose
23: 
24: Defines consistent styling rules for Rust used as napi-rs, WASM/WASI, or sidecar compute modules alongside the existing TypeScript/Node MCP backend.
25: 
26: The primary requirement is not merely idiomatic Rust. Rust implementations MUST preserve the observable TypeScript contract byte for byte, including six-decimal numeric behavior, stable comparator chains, deterministic identifiers, key order, serialized number spelling, DTO shapes, and JavaScript error behavior.
27: 
28: ### When to Use
29: 
30: - Writing new Rust files under an OpenCode workspace
31: - Extracting measured compute kernels from TypeScript
32: - Implementing napi-rs, WASM/WASI, or sidecar adapters
33: - Reviewing Rust naming, formatting, ownership, or module organization
34: - Maintaining byte-for-byte parity with a TypeScript oracle
35: - Defining Rust DTOs consumed by JavaScript or TypeScript
36: 
37: ### Repository Non-Negotiables
38: 
39: 1. **The interop boundary is a stability contract.**
40:    - Exported names, DTO fields, optionality, discriminants, numeric representations, buffer ownership, generated declarations, error codes, messages, and throw-versus-rejection behavior are versioned contracts.
41:    - Contract protected: **DTO/ABI and JavaScript error-shape parity**.
42:    - Keep MCP transport, public tool schemas, daemon wiring, feature flags, and fallback selection in TypeScript.
43:    - Keep napi-rs, wasm-bindgen, Node handles, and runtime values out of the pure core.
44: 
45: 2. **Determinism means byte-for-byte TypeScript parity.**
46:    - The release assertion is equivalent to comparing the bytes emitted by the TypeScript oracle and Rust boundary.
47:    - Preserve numeric operations independently. TypeScript `toFixed(6)`, scaled `Math.round`, and fixed-six textual formatting are not interchangeable.
48:    - Preserve comparator chains, terminal tie-breaks, identifier preimages, UTF-8 encoding, delimiters, hash algorithms, lowercase hexadecimal output, truncation, key order, omission behavior, and serialized number spelling.
49:    - Contracts protected: **six-decimal score parity, stable sort parity, deterministic-ID parity, deterministic iteration order, and serialized-output parity**.
50: 
51: 3. **No `unsafe` without a documented invariant and tests.**
52:    - Pure-core crates use `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`.
53:    - Boundary crates use `#![deny(unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn)]`.
54:    - Every permitted unsafe block requires an adjacent `// SAFETY:` explanation and tests that exercise both valid inputs and challenged preconditions.
55:    - Contract protected: **FFI memory safety and boundary integrity**.
56: 
57: 4. **Panics are not boundary errors.**
58:    - JavaScript-controlled input must not reach `unwrap`, `expect`, unchecked indexing, explicit `panic!`, or assertion-dependent validation.
59:    - Recoverable failures use typed `Result` values and exhaustive adapter mappings.
60:    - Contract protected: **Node process survival, WASM trap avoidance, and JavaScript error-shape parity**.
61: 
62: ---
63: 
64: ## 2. FILE HEADER FORMAT
65: 
66: All Rust source files MUST begin with a module header block identifying the module.
67: 
68: Crate roots add crate-level safety and documentation attributes before the module header. Ordinary module files begin directly with the header.
69: 
70: ### Module Template
71: 
72: ```rust
73: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
74: // MODULE: [Module Name]
75: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
76: ```
77: 
78: ### Pure-Core Crate Root Template
79: 
80: ```rust
81: #![forbid(unsafe_code)]
82: 
83: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
84: // MODULE: Deterministic Ranking Core
85: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
86: ```
87: 
88: ### Boundary Crate Root Template
89: 
90: ```rust
91: #![deny(unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn)]
92: 
93: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
94: // MODULE: Node.js Ranking Adapter
95: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
96: ```
97: 
98: ### Requirements
99: 
100: - Box width: 67 characters total
101: - Module name: Left-aligned within the header
102: - Pure core: `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` at the crate root
103: - FFI or runtime adapter: `#![deny(unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn)]` at the crate root
104: - Crate attributes: Before the module header
105: - Module documentation: After the module header and before imports
106: - Imports: After module documentation
107: - No generated timestamp, packet identifier, ticket identifier, or transient ownership marker
108: - No copied TypeScript file path unless it is part of a durable compatibility contract
109: 
110: **Rationale**: The crate-level attribute states the safety policy enforced by the compiler. The module header makes mixed TypeScript/Rust workspaces easier to navigate without embedding transient project-management data.
111: 
112: ### Full Header Example
113: 
114: ```rust
115: #![forbid(unsafe_code)]
116: 
117: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
118: // MODULE: Deterministic Ranking Core
119: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
120: 
121: //! Computes canonical ranking output compatible with the TypeScript oracle.
122: //!
123: //! Sorting and numeric normalization in this crate protect byte-for-byte
124: //! parity across native and WASM targets.
125: 
126: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
127: // 1. IMPORTS
128: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
129: 
130: use std::cmp::Ordering;
131: 
132: use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
133: 
134: use crate::error::CoreError;
135: use crate::ids::SymbolId;
136: ```
137: 
138: ### Binary Entry Point Template
139: 
140: Sidecar binaries MAY permit `anyhow` at the outermost application shell. Domain and parity-sensitive operations remain typed in the core.
141: 
142: ```rust
143: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
144: // MODULE: Ranking Sidecar
145: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
146: 
147: use anyhow::Context;
148: 
149: use ranking_core::run_request;
150: 
151: fn main() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
152:     let input = std::fs::read_to_string("/dev/stdin")
153:         .context("failed to read sidecar request")?;
154: 
155:     let output = run_request(&input)
156:         .context("failed to execute ranking request")?;
157: 
158:     println!("{output}");
159:     Ok(())
160: }
161: ```
162: 
163: `anyhow` is acceptable here because `main` is the outer application shell. It is not acceptable in the public API of `ranking_core`.
164:

12: 
13: # Naming Conventions
14: 
15: Formatting standards, naming conventions, and TypeScript interoperability rules for Rust files in the OpenCode development environment.
16: 
17: ---
18: 
19: ## 1. OVERVIEW
20: 
21: ### Purpose
22: 
23: Gives the naming rules for every Rust item, including the JavaScript-visible and DTO field names that cross the interop boundary.
24: 
25: ### When to Use
26: 
27: - Naming a type, trait, function, constant or module
28: - Choosing a getter, conversion prefix or boolean name
29: - Naming a JavaScript-visible export or a DTO field
30: - Checking a name against the summary table
31: 
32: ---
33: 
34: ## 2. NAMING CONVENTIONS
35: 
36: ### Types and Traits
37: 
38: **Style**: `UpperCamelCase`
39: 
40: ```rust
41: struct SearchResult {
42:     score: f64,
43: }
44: 
45: enum MemoryState {
46:     Active,
47:     Archived,
48: }
49: 
50: trait EmbeddingProvider {
51:     fn embed(&self, input: &str) -> Result<Vec<f32>, EmbedError>;
52: }
53: 
54: #[derive(Debug)]
55: struct EmbedError;
56: ```
57: 
58: Treat acronyms as words:
59: 
60: ```rust
61: struct UuidParser;
62: struct HttpClient;
63: struct WasmAdapter;
64: struct NapiErrorMapper;
65: ```
66: 
67: Do not use `UUIDParser`, `HTTPClient`, or `WASMAdapter`.
68: 
69: ### Functions, Methods, Variables, and Modules
70: 
71: **Style**: `snake_case`
72: 
73: ```rust
74: mod score_normalization;
75: 
76: fn calculate_decay_score(age_seconds: u64) -> f64 {
77:     1.0 / (1.0 + age_seconds as f64)
78: }
79: 
80: let search_results = Vec::<String>::new();
81: let should_retry = false;
82: ```
83: 
84: ### Constants and Statics
85: 
86: **Style**: `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE`
87: 
88: ```rust
89: const MAX_QUERY_LENGTH: usize = 10_000;
90: const SCORE_SCALE: f64 = 1_000_000.0;
91: static SUPPORTED_TARGETS: &[&str] = &["native", "wasm"];
92: ```
93: 
94: A local immutable binding remains `snake_case`; not every `let` binding is a constant.
95: 
96: ### Generic Parameters
97: 
98: Use short uppercase names for familiar generic roles and descriptive `UpperCamelCase` names when multiple parameters would otherwise be ambiguous.
99: 
100: ```rust
101: fn identity<T>(value: T) -> T {
102:     value
103: }
104: 
105: fn transform<Input, Output, Error>(
106:     input: Input,
107:     operation: impl FnOnce(Input) -> Result<Output, Error>,
108: ) -> Result<Output, Error> {
109:     operation(input)
110: }
111: ```
112: 
113: ### Getter Names
114: 
115: Omit `get_` for ordinary, side-effect-free accessors.
116: 
117: ```rust
118: struct Candidate {
119:     id: String,
120:     score: f64,
121: }
122: 
123: impl Candidate {
124:     fn id(&self) -> &str {
125:         &self.id
126:     }
127: 
128:     fn score(&self) -> f64 {
129:         self.score
130:     }
131: }
132: ```
133: 
134: Use a verb when the operation performs work, I/O, mutation, or validation:
135: 
136: ```rust
137: fn load_config() -> Result<String, std::io::Error> {
138:     std::fs::read_to_string("config.json")
139: }
140: 
141: fn validate_score(value: f64) -> Result<f64, &'static str> {
142:     value.is_finite().then_some(value).ok_or("score must be finite")
143: }
144: ```
145: 
146: ### Conversion Method Prefixes
147: 
148: | Prefix | Meaning | Example |
149: |--------|---------|---------|
150: | `as_` | Cheap borrowed view | `as_str()` |
151: | `to_` | Work or allocation | `to_canonical_json()` |
152: | `into_` | Consumes `self` | `into_inner()` |
153: 
154: ```rust
155: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
156: struct SymbolId(String);
157: 
158: impl SymbolId {
159:     fn as_str(&self) -> &str {
160:         &self.0
161:     }
162: 
163:     fn to_lowercase_hex(&self) -> String {
164:         self.0.to_ascii_lowercase()
165:     }
166: 
167:     fn into_inner(self) -> String {
168:         self.0
169:     }
170: }
171: ```
172: 
173: Do not name an allocating clone `as_bytes_owned`; use `to_bytes`. Do not name a borrowed view `to_str`; use `as_str`.
174: 
175: ### Newtypes
176: 
177: Use private-field newtypes for validated or parity-sensitive primitives.
178: 
179: ```rust
180: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash)]
181: pub struct SymbolId(String);
182: 
183: impl SymbolId {
184:     #[must_use]
185:     pub fn as_str(&self) -> &str {
186:         &self.0
187:     }
188: }
189: ```
190: 
191: Recommended newtypes include:
192: 
193: - `SymbolId` for deterministic identifiers
194: - `SkillId` for validated identifiers
195: - `FiniteScore` for finite values and centralized quantization
196: - `Rank` where zero-based and one-based semantics differ
197: 
198: Derive only traits whose semantics are correct for the domain. In particular, do not derive `Eq` or `Ord` for raw floating-point fields.
199: 
200: ### Boolean Names
201: 
202: Rust predicates SHOULD read naturally:
203: 
204: ```rust
205: let is_valid = true;
206: let has_results = !results.is_empty();
207: let can_retry = attempts < MAX_RETRIES;
208: let should_emit_metadata = options.include_metadata;
209: ```
210: 
211: Predicate methods MAY omit `is_` when Rust convention is clearer:
212: 
213: ```rust
214: fn empty(&self) -> bool {
215:     self.items.is_empty()
216: }
217: ```
218: 
219: Prefer established standard-library vocabulary such as `is_empty`, `contains`, and `starts_with`.
220: 
221: ### File and Module Names
222: 
223: **Style**: `snake_case` with `.rs`
224: 
225: ```text
226: trigger_lookup.rs
227: vector_index.rs
228: path_security.rs
229: embedding_provider.rs
230: ```
231: 
232: Crate package names use `kebab-case` in `Cargo.toml`; the Rust crate identifier is automatically exposed with underscores.
233: 
234: ```toml
235: [package]
236: name = "ranking-core"
237: ```
238: 
239: ```rust
240: use ranking_core::rank_candidates;
241: ```
242: 
243: ### JavaScript-Visible Names
244: 
245: Core Rust names remain idiomatic. Preserve established JavaScript `camelCase` names with adapter attributes.
246: 
247: ```rust
248: use napi_derive::napi;
249: 
250: #[napi(js_name = "calculateDecayScore")]
251: pub fn calculate_decay_score(age_seconds: u32) -> f64 {
252:     1.0 / (1.0 + f64::from(age_seconds))
253: }
254: ```
255: 
256: For wasm-bindgen:
257: 
258: ```rust
259: use wasm_bindgen::prelude::*;
260: 
261: #[wasm_bindgen(js_name = calculateDecayScore)]
262: pub fn calculate_decay_score(age_seconds: u32) -> f64 {
263:     1.0 / (1.0 + f64::from(age_seconds))
264: }
265: ```
266: 
267: Do not contaminate core naming with JavaScript casing:
268: 
269: ```rust
270: // Incorrect Rust API shape:
271: fn calculateDecayScore(_age_seconds: u32) -> f64 {
272:     0.0
273: }
274: ```
275: 
276: ### DTO Field Names
277: 
278: Boundary DTO fields and serialized keys MUST match the TypeScript contract exactly. Use rename attributes instead of non-idiomatic core fields.
279: 
280: ```rust
281: use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
282: 
283: #[derive(Debug, Deserialize, Serialize)]
284: #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
285: struct SearchOptionsDto {
286:     max_results: u32,
287:     include_metadata: bool,
288: }
289: ```
290: 
291: Use explicit field renames when the contract is irregular:
292: 
293: ```rust
294: use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
295: 
296: #[derive(Debug, Deserialize, Serialize)]
297: struct ModelDto {
298:     #[serde(rename = "modelID")]
299:     model_id: String,
300: }
301: ```
302: 
303: ### Naming Summary Table

305: | Element | Convention | Example |
306: |---------|------------|---------|
307: | Structs | `UpperCamelCase` | `SearchResult` |
308: | Enums | `UpperCamelCase` | `MemoryState` |

310: | Traits | `UpperCamelCase` | `EmbeddingProvider` |

13: # Naming Conventions
14: 
15: Formatting standards, naming conventions, and TypeScript interoperability rules for Rust files in the OpenCode development environment.
16: 
17: ---
18: 
19: ## 1. OVERVIEW
20: 
21: ### Purpose
22: 
23: Gives the naming rules for every Rust item, including the JavaScript-visible and DTO field names that cross the interop boundary.
24: 
25: ### When to Use
26: 
27: - Naming a type, trait, function, constant or module
28: - Choosing a getter, conversion prefix or boolean name
29: - Naming a JavaScript-visible export or a DTO field

31: 
32: ---
33: 
34: ## 2. NAMING CONVENTIONS
35: 
36: ### Types and Traits
37: 
38: **Style**: `UpperCamelCase`
39: 
40: ```rust
41: struct SearchResult {
42:     score: f64,
43: }
44: 
45: enum MemoryState {
46:     Active,
47:     Archived,
48: }
49: 
50: trait EmbeddingProvider {
51:     fn embed(&self, input: &str) -> Result<Vec<f32>, EmbedError>;
52: }
53: 
54: #[derive(Debug)]
55: struct EmbedError;
56: ```
57: 
58: Treat acronyms as words:
59: 
60: ```rust
61: struct UuidParser;
62: struct HttpClient;
63: struct WasmAdapter;
64: struct NapiErrorMapper;
65: ```
66: 
67: Do not use `UUIDParser`, `HTTPClient`, or `WASMAdapter`.
68: 
69: ### Functions, Methods, Variables, and Modules
70: 
71: **Style**: `snake_case`
72: 
73: ```rust
74: mod score_normalization;
75: 
76: fn calculate_decay_score(age_seconds: u64) -> f64 {
77:     1.0 / (1.0 + age_seconds as f64)
78: }
79: 
80: let search_results = Vec::<String>::new();
81: let should_retry = false;
82: ```
83: 
84: ### Constants and Statics
85: 
86: **Style**: `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE`
87: 
88: ```rust
89: const MAX_QUERY_LENGTH: usize = 10_000;
90: const SCORE_SCALE: f64 = 1_000_000.0;
91: static SUPPORTED_TARGETS: &[&str] = &["native", "wasm"];
92: ```
93: 
94: A local immutable binding remains `snake_case`; not every `let` binding is a constant.
95: 
96: ### Generic Parameters
97: 
98: Use short uppercase names for familiar generic roles and descriptive `UpperCamelCase` names when multiple parameters would otherwise be ambiguous.
99: 
100: ```rust
101: fn identity<T>(value: T) -> T {
102:     value
103: }
104: 
105: fn transform<Input, Output, Error>(
106:     input: Input,
107:     operation: impl FnOnce(Input) -> Result<Output, Error>,
108: ) -> Result<Output, Error> {
109:     operation(input)
110: }
111: ```
112: 
113: ### Getter Names
114: 
115: Omit `get_` for ordinary, side-effect-free accessors.
116: 
117: ```rust
118: struct Candidate {
119:     id: String,
120:     score: f64,
121: }
122: 
123: impl Candidate {
124:     fn id(&self) -> &str {
125:         &self.id
126:     }
127: 
128:     fn score(&self) -> f64 {
129:         self.score
130:     }
131: }
132: ```
133: 
134: Use a verb when the operation performs work, I/O, mutation, or validation:
135: 
136: ```rust
137: fn load_config() -> Result<String, std::io::Error> {
138:     std::fs::read_to_string("config.json")
139: }
140: 
141: fn validate_score(value: f64) -> Result<f64, &'static str> {
142:     value.is_finite().then_some(value).ok_or("score must be finite")
143: }
144: ```
145: 
146: ### Conversion Method Prefixes
147: 
148: | Prefix | Meaning | Example |
149: |--------|---------|---------|
150: | `as_` | Cheap borrowed view | `as_str()` |
151: | `to_` | Work or allocation | `to_canonical_json()` |
152: | `into_` | Consumes `self` | `into_inner()` |
153: 
154: ```rust
155: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
156: struct SymbolId(String);
157: 
158: impl SymbolId {
159:     fn as_str(&self) -> &str {
160:         &self.0
161:     }
162: 
163:     fn to_lowercase_hex(&self) -> String {
164:         self.0.to_ascii_lowercase()
165:     }
166: 
167:     fn into_inner(self) -> String {
168:         self.0
169:     }
170: }
171: ```
172: 
173: Do not name an allocating clone `as_bytes_owned`; use `to_bytes`. Do not name a borrowed view `to_str`; use `as_str`.
174: 
175: ### Newtypes
176: 
177: Use private-field newtypes for validated or parity-sensitive primitives.
178: 
179: ```rust
180: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash)]
181: pub struct SymbolId(String);
182: 
183: impl SymbolId {
184:     #[must_use]
185:     pub fn as_str(&self) -> &str {
186:         &self.0
187:     }
188: }
189: ```
190: 
191: Recommended newtypes include:
192: 
193: - `SymbolId` for deterministic identifiers
194: - `SkillId` for validated identifiers
195: - `FiniteScore` for finite values and centralized quantization
196: - `Rank` where zero-based and one-based semantics differ
197: 
198: Derive only traits whose semantics are correct for the domain. In particular, do not derive `Eq` or `Ord` for raw floating-point fields.
199: 
200: ### Boolean Names
201: 
202: Rust predicates SHOULD read naturally:
203: 
204: ```rust
205: let is_valid = true;
206: let has_results = !results.is_empty();
207: let can_retry = attempts < MAX_RETRIES;
208: let should_emit_metadata = options.include_metadata;
209: ```
210: 
211: Predicate methods MAY omit `is_` when Rust convention is clearer:
212: 
213: ```rust
214: fn empty(&self) -> bool {
215:     self.items.is_empty()
216: }
217: ```
218: 
219: Prefer established standard-library vocabulary such as `is_empty`, `contains`, and `starts_with`.
220: 
221: ### File and Module Names
222: 
223: **Style**: `snake_case` with `.rs`
224: 
225: ```text
226: trigger_lookup.rs
227: vector_index.rs
228: path_security.rs
229: embedding_provider.rs
230: ```
231: 
232: Crate package names use `kebab-case` in `Cargo.toml`; the Rust crate identifier is automatically exposed with underscores.
233: 
234: ```toml
235: [package]
236: name = "ranking-core"
237: ```
238: 
239: ```rust
240: use ranking_core::rank_candidates;
241: ```
242: 
243: ### JavaScript-Visible Names
244: 
245: Core Rust names remain idiomatic. Preserve established JavaScript `camelCase` names with adapter attributes.
246: 
247: ```rust
248: use napi_derive::napi;
249: 
250: #[napi(js_name = "calculateDecayScore")]
251: pub fn calculate_decay_score(age_seconds: u32) -> f64 {
252:     1.0 / (1.0 + f64::from(age_seconds))
253: }
254: ```
255: 
256: For wasm-bindgen:
257: 
258: ```rust
259: use wasm_bindgen::prelude::*;
260: 
261: #[wasm_bindgen(js_name = calculateDecayScore)]
262: pub fn calculate_decay_score(age_seconds: u32) -> f64 {
263:     1.0 / (1.0 + f64::from(age_seconds))
264: }
265: ```
266: 
267: Do not contaminate core naming with JavaScript casing:
268: 
269: ```rust
270: // Incorrect Rust API shape:
271: fn calculateDecayScore(_age_seconds: u32) -> f64 {
272:     0.0
273: }
274: ```
275: 
276: ### DTO Field Names
277: 
278: Boundary DTO fields and serialized keys MUST match the TypeScript contract exactly. Use rename attributes instead of non-idiomatic core fields.
279: 
280: ```rust
281: use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
282: 
283: #[derive(Debug, Deserialize, Serialize)]
284: #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
285: struct SearchOptionsDto {
286:     max_results: u32,
287:     include_metadata: bool,
288: }
289: ```
290: 
291: Use explicit field renames when the contract is irregular:
292: 
293: ```rust
294: use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
295: 
296: #[derive(Debug, Deserialize, Serialize)]
297: struct ModelDto {
298:     #[serde(rename = "modelID")]
299:     model_id: String,
300: }
301: ```
302: 
303: ### Naming Summary Table
304: 
305: | Element | Convention | Example |
306: |---------|------------|---------|
307: | Structs | `UpperCamelCase` | `SearchResult` |
308: | Enums | `UpperCamelCase` | `MemoryState` |
309: | Enum variants | `UpperCamelCase` | `MemoryState::LongTerm` |
310: | Traits | `UpperCamelCase` | `EmbeddingProvider` |
311: | Type aliases | `UpperCamelCase` | `ScoreMap` |
312: | Generic parameters | Uppercase/`UpperCamelCase` | `T`, `Input` |
313: | Functions | `snake_case` | `load_config` |
314: | Methods | `snake_case` | `canonical_bytes` |

12: 
13: # Toolchain, Compilation Baseline & Project Structure
14: 
15: Formatting standards, naming conventions, and TypeScript interoperability rules for Rust files in the OpenCode development environment.
16: 
17: ---
18: 
19: ## 1. OVERVIEW
20: 
21: ### Purpose
22: 
23: Fixes the workspace toolchain, compilation baseline and source and module layout that every Rust crate in the workspace inherits.
24: 
25: ### When to Use
26: 
27: - Setting up or reviewing a workspace `Cargo.toml`, edition, MSRV or release profile
28: - Deciding feature flags or compilation targets
29: - Laying out a Rust file's sections, modules or workspace crates
30: - Checking module responsibilities and visibility
31: 
32: ---
33: 
34: ## 2. EDITION, TOOLCHAIN, AND COMPILATION BASELINE
35: 
36: ### Workspace Configuration Is Authoritative
37: 
38: Rust crates MUST inherit the edition, minimum supported Rust version, dependency versions, lint policy, and release policy from the workspace root where Cargo supports inheritance.
39: 
40: ```toml
41: # Cargo.toml
42: [workspace]
43: resolver = "2"
44: members = [
45:   "crates/core",
46:   "crates/napi",
47:   "crates/wasm",
48: ]
49: 
50: [workspace.package]
51: edition = "2024"
52: rust-version = "1.85"
53: license = "MIT"
54: 
55: [workspace.dependencies]
56: serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }
57: serde_json = "1"
58: thiserror = "2"
59: 
60: [workspace.lints.rust]
61: unsafe_code = "deny"
62: 
63: [workspace.lints.clippy]
64: all = "warn"
65: pedantic = "warn"
66: ```
67: 
68: Member crates inherit the shared policy:
69: 
70: ```toml
71: # crates/core/Cargo.toml
72: [package]
73: name = "ranking-core"
74: version = "0.1.0"
75: edition.workspace = true
76: rust-version.workspace = true
77: license.workspace = true
78: 
79: [dependencies]
80: serde.workspace = true
81: serde_json.workspace = true
82: thiserror.workspace = true
83: 
84: [lints]
85: workspace = true
86: ```
87: 
88: ### Edition Rules
89: 
90: - Use the edition selected by the owning workspace.
91: - Do not set a different edition in an individual member without a documented compatibility requirement.
92: - Do not rely on implicit edition behavior when generated bindings, macros, or build tooling require a specific edition.
93: - Keep edition upgrades workspace-wide so native, WASM, sidecar, tests, and examples compile under one language baseline.
94: 
95: ### Minimum Supported Rust Version
96: 
97: The workspace `rust-version` is a compilation contract.
98: 
99: - Do not use syntax or standard-library APIs newer than the declared version.
100: - Do not raise `rust-version` in one crate only.
101: - Verify the declared minimum version in CI, not only the latest stable toolchain.
102: - Pin toolchain components when reproducibility requires a checked-in `rust-toolchain.toml`.
103: 
104: ```toml
105: # rust-toolchain.toml
106: [toolchain]
107: channel = "1.85.0"
108: components = ["clippy", "rustfmt"]
109: profile = "minimal"
110: targets = ["wasm32-unknown-unknown"]
111: ```
112: 
113: The exact channel and targets must match the repository's active workspace policy. Do not copy this example without reconciling it with the owning `Cargo.toml`.
114: 
115: ### Compilation Baseline
116: 
117: All Rust work MUST pass the workspace-equivalent of:
118: 
119: ```bash
120: cargo fmt --all --check
121: cargo check --workspace --all-targets
122: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
123: cargo test --workspace
124: ```
125: 
126: Target-specific crates also require their target build:
127: 
128: ```bash
129: cargo check -p ranking-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown
130: cargo build -p ranking-napi --release
131: ```
132: 
133: ### Feature Rules
134: 
135: Separate native and WASM integrations so unsupported combinations are not accidentally compiled together.
136: 
137: ```toml
138: [features]
139: default = []
140: native = ["dep:napi", "dep:napi-derive"]
141: wasm = ["dep:wasm-bindgen"]
142: 
143: [dependencies]
144: napi = { version = "3", optional = true }
145: napi-derive = { version = "3", optional = true }
146: wasm-bindgen = { version = "0.2", optional = true }
147: ```
148: 
149: Do not place mutually incompatible adapter dependencies in the pure core. Prefer separate adapter crates over a dense matrix of target-specific conditionals.
150: 
151: ### Release Semantics
152: 
153: Do not depend on debug-only overflow checks, assertion behavior, or profile-specific floating-point transformations.
154: 
155: ```rust
156: pub fn checked_increment(value: u32) -> Result<u32, &'static str> {
157:     value.checked_add(1).ok_or("counter overflow")
158: }
159: ```
160: 
161: Explicit checked behavior protects parity across development, release, native, and WASM builds.
162: 
163: ---
164: 
165: ## 3. SECTION ORGANIZATION
166: 
167: Large Rust files use numbered section dividers. Small modules do not need dividers when ordinary Rust structure is clearer.
168: 
169: ### Section Divider Template
170: 
171: ```rust
172: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
173: // 1. [SECTION NAME]
174: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
175: ```
176: 
177: Use one divider format consistently within a file. Rust source uses line-comment dividers; do not alternate between line and block dividers.
178: 
179: ### Standard Source Order
180: 
181: | Order | Section Name | Purpose |
182: |-------|--------------|---------|
183: | 1 | IMPORTS | Standard-library, third-party, and crate imports |
184: | 2 | CONSTANTS | Stable configuration and numeric constants |
185: | 3 | TYPES | Structs, enums, traits, and newtypes |
186: | 4 | CONVERSIONS | `From` and `TryFrom` implementations |
187: | 5 | HELPERS | Private utility functions |
188: | 6 | CORE LOGIC | Public and private implementation |
189: | 7 | TESTS | Unit tests in `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` |
190: 
191: Number sections from the first divider actually present. The module header does not count.
192: 
193: ### Complete Organization Example
194: 
195: ```rust
196: #![forbid(unsafe_code)]
197: 
198: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
199: // MODULE: Score Normalization
200: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
201: 
202: use std::cmp::Ordering;
203: 
204: use thiserror::Error;
205: 
206: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
207: // 1. CONSTANTS
208: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
209: 
210: const SCORE_SCALE: f64 = 1_000_000.0;
211: 
212: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
213: // 2. TYPES
214: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
215: 
216: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
217: pub struct FiniteScore(f64);
218: 
219: #[derive(Debug, Error, PartialEq)]
220: pub enum ScoreError {
221:     #[error("score must be finite")]
222:     NonFinite,
223: }
224: 
225: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
226: // 3. CONVERSIONS
227: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
228: 
229: impl TryFrom<f64> for FiniteScore {
230:     type Error = ScoreError;
231: 
232:     fn try_from(value: f64) -> Result<Self, Self::Error> {
233:         if value.is_finite() {
234:             Ok(Self(value))
235:         } else {
236:             Err(ScoreError::NonFinite)
237:         }
238:     }
239: }
240: 
241: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
242: // 4. CORE LOGIC
243: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
244: 
245: impl FiniteScore {
246:     #[must_use]
247:     pub fn value(self) -> f64 {
248:         self.0
249:     }
250: 
251:     #[must_use]
252:     pub fn scaled_round(self) -> f64 {
253:         (self.0 * SCORE_SCALE).round() / SCORE_SCALE
254:     }
255: 
256:     #[must_use]
257:     pub fn total_cmp(self, other: Self) -> Ordering {
258:         self.0.total_cmp(&other.0)
259:     }
260: }
261: 
262: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
263: // 5. TESTS
264: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
265: 
266: #[cfg(test)]
267: mod tests {
268:     use super::FiniteScore;
269:
