13: # Toolchain, Compilation Baseline & Project Structure
14: 
15: Formatting standards, naming conventions, and TypeScript interoperability rules for Rust files in the OpenCode development environment.
16: 
17: ---
18: 
19: ## 1. OVERVIEW
20: 
21: ### Purpose
22: 
23: Fixes the workspace toolchain, compilation baseline and source and module layout that every Rust crate in the workspace inherits.
24: 
25: ### When to Use
26: 
27: - Setting up or reviewing a workspace `Cargo.toml`, edition, MSRV or release profile
28: - Deciding feature flags or compilation targets
29: - Laying out a Rust file's sections, modules or workspace crates
30: - Checking module responsibilities and visibility
31: 
32: ---
33: 
34: ## 2. EDITION, TOOLCHAIN, AND COMPILATION BASELINE
35: 
36: ### Workspace Configuration Is Authoritative
37: 
38: Rust crates MUST inherit the edition, minimum supported Rust version, dependency versions, lint policy, and release policy from the workspace root where Cargo supports inheritance.
39: 
40: ```toml
41: # Cargo.toml
42: [workspace]
43: resolver = "2"
44: members = [
45:   "crates/core",
46:   "crates/napi",
47:   "crates/wasm",
48: ]
49: 
50: [workspace.package]
51: edition = "2024"
52: rust-version = "1.85"
53: license = "MIT"
54: 
55: [workspace.dependencies]
56: serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }
57: serde_json = "1"
58: thiserror = "2"
59: 
60: [workspace.lints.rust]
61: unsafe_code = "deny"
62: 
63: [workspace.lints.clippy]
64: all = "warn"
65: pedantic = "warn"
66: ```
67: 
68: Member crates inherit the shared policy:
69: 
70: ```toml
71: # crates/core/Cargo.toml
72: [package]
73: name = "ranking-core"
74: version = "0.1.0"
75: edition.workspace = true
76: rust-version.workspace = true
77: license.workspace = true
78: 
79: [dependencies]
80: serde.workspace = true
81: serde_json.workspace = true
82: thiserror.workspace = true
83: 
84: [lints]
85: workspace = true
86: ```
87: 
88: ### Edition Rules
89: 
90: - Use the edition selected by the owning workspace.
91: - Do not set a different edition in an individual member without a documented compatibility requirement.
92: - Do not rely on implicit edition behavior when generated bindings, macros, or build tooling require a specific edition.
93: - Keep edition upgrades workspace-wide so native, WASM, sidecar, tests, and examples compile under one language baseline.
94: 
95: ### Minimum Supported Rust Version
96: 
97: The workspace `rust-version` is a compilation contract.
98: 
99: - Do not use syntax or standard-library APIs newer than the declared version.
100: - Do not raise `rust-version` in one crate only.
101: - Verify the declared minimum version in CI, not only the latest stable toolchain.
102: - Pin toolchain components when reproducibility requires a checked-in `rust-toolchain.toml`.
103: 
104: ```toml
105: # rust-toolchain.toml
106: [toolchain]
107: channel = "1.85.0"
108: components = ["clippy", "rustfmt"]
109: profile = "minimal"
110: targets = ["wasm32-unknown-unknown"]
111: ```
112: 
113: The exact channel and targets must match the repository's active workspace policy. Do not copy this example without reconciling it with the owning `Cargo.toml`.
114: 
115: ### Compilation Baseline
116: 
117: All Rust work MUST pass the workspace-equivalent of:
118: 
119: ```bash
120: cargo fmt --all --check
121: cargo check --workspace --all-targets
122: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
123: cargo test --workspace
124: ```
125: 
126: Target-specific crates also require their target build:
127: 
128: ```bash
129: cargo check -p ranking-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown
130: cargo build -p ranking-napi --release
131: ```
132: 
133: ### Feature Rules
134: 
135: Separate native and WASM integrations so unsupported combinations are not accidentally compiled together.
136: 
137: ```toml
138: [features]
139: default = []
140: native = ["dep:napi", "dep:napi-derive"]
141: wasm = ["dep:wasm-bindgen"]
142: 
143: [dependencies]
144: napi = { version = "3", optional = true }
145: napi-derive = { version = "3", optional = true }
146: wasm-bindgen = { version = "0.2", optional = true }
147: ```
148: 
149: Do not place mutually incompatible adapter dependencies in the pure core. Prefer separate adapter crates over a dense matrix of target-specific conditionals.
150: 
151: ### Release Semantics
152: 
153: Do not depend on debug-only overflow checks, assertion behavior, or profile-specific floating-point transformations.
154: 
155: ```rust
156: pub fn checked_increment(value: u32) -> Result<u32, &'static str> {
157:     value.checked_add(1).ok_or("counter overflow")
158: }
159: ```
160: 
161: Explicit checked behavior protects parity across development, release, native, and WASM builds.
162: 
163: ---
164: 
165: ## 3. SECTION ORGANIZATION
166: 
167: Large Rust files use numbered section dividers. Small modules do not need dividers when ordinary Rust structure is clearer.
168: 
169: ### Section Divider Template
170: 
171: ```rust
172: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
173: // 1. [SECTION NAME]
174: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
175: ```
176: 
177: Use one divider format consistently within a file. Rust source uses line-comment dividers; do not alternate between line and block dividers.
178: 
179: ### Standard Source Order
180: 
181: | Order | Section Name | Purpose |
182: |-------|--------------|---------|
183: | 1 | IMPORTS | Standard-library, third-party, and crate imports |
184: | 2 | CONSTANTS | Stable configuration and numeric constants |
185: | 3 | TYPES | Structs, enums, traits, and newtypes |
186: | 4 | CONVERSIONS | `From` and `TryFrom` implementations |
187: | 5 | HELPERS | Private utility functions |
188: | 6 | CORE LOGIC | Public and private implementation |
189: | 7 | TESTS | Unit tests in `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` |
190: 
191: Number sections from the first divider actually present. The module header does not count.
192: 
193: ### Complete Organization Example
194: 
195: ```rust
196: #![forbid(unsafe_code)]
197: 
198: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
199: // MODULE: Score Normalization
200: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
201: 
202: use std::cmp::Ordering;
203: 
204: use thiserror::Error;
205: 
206: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
207: // 1. CONSTANTS
208: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
209: 
210: const SCORE_SCALE: f64 = 1_000_000.0;
211: 
212: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
213: // 2. TYPES
214: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
215: 
216: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
217: pub struct FiniteScore(f64);
218: 
219: #[derive(Debug, Error, PartialEq)]
220: pub enum ScoreError {
221:     #[error("score must be finite")]
222:     NonFinite,
223: }
224: 
225: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
226: // 3. CONVERSIONS
227: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
228: 
229: impl TryFrom<f64> for FiniteScore {
230:     type Error = ScoreError;
231: 
232:     fn try_from(value: f64) -> Result<Self, Self::Error> {
233:         if value.is_finite() {
234:             Ok(Self(value))
235:         } else {
236:             Err(ScoreError::NonFinite)
237:         }
238:     }
239: }
240: 
241: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
242: // 4. CORE LOGIC
243: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
244: 
245: impl FiniteScore {
246:     #[must_use]
247:     pub fn value(self) -> f64 {
248:         self.0
249:     }
250: 
251:     #[must_use]
252:     pub fn scaled_round(self) -> f64 {
253:         (self.0 * SCORE_SCALE).round() / SCORE_SCALE
254:     }
255: 
256:     #[must_use]
257:     pub fn total_cmp(self, other: Self) -> Ordering {
258:         self.0.total_cmp(&other.0)
259:     }
260: }
261: 
262: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
263: // 5. TESTS
264: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
265: 
266: #[cfg(test)]
267: mod tests {
268:     use super::FiniteScore;
269: 
270:     #[test]
271:     fn rejects_non_finite_scores() {
272:         assert!(FiniteScore::try_from(f64::NAN).is_err());
273:     }
274: }
275: ```
276: 
277: ### Module and Workspace Layout
278: 
279: Use a pure core with thin runtime adapters:
280: 
281: ```text
282: Cargo.toml
283: Cargo.lock
284: rust-toolchain.toml
285: crates/
286:   core/
287:     Cargo.toml
288:     src/
289:       lib.rs
290:       dto.rs
291:       error.rs
292:       ids.rs
293:       ranking.rs
294:   napi/
295:     Cargo.toml
296:     src/
297:       lib.rs
298:   wasm/
299:     Cargo.toml
300:     src/
301:       lib.rs
302:   sidecar/
303:     Cargo.toml
304:     src/
305:       main.rs
306: ```
307: 
308: ### Module Responsibilities
309: 
310: - `core` owns algorithms, validation, normalization, numeric parity, sorting, hashing, deterministic IDs, and transport-neutral domain types.
311: - `napi` owns Node conversion, generated TypeScript declarations, JavaScript error mapping, and thread-affinity rules.
312: - `wasm` owns JavaScript/WASM conversion, trap avoidance, and WASM-specific exports.
313: - `sidecar` owns framing, process I/O, and outer-shell diagnostics.
314: - Adapters MUST NOT duplicate scoring, sorting, hashing, rounding, identifier generation, or business validation.
315: - Use one workspace lockfile.
316: - Keep native and WASM dependencies out of the core dependency graph.
317: 
318: ### Module Visibility
319: 
320: Default to private modules and private fields. Export the smallest stable API required by adapters.
321: 
322: ```rust
323: mod ids;
324: mod ranking;
325: 
326: pub use ids::SymbolId;
327: pub use ranking::{rank_candidates, Candidate, RankedCandidate};
328: ```
329: 
330: Avoid broad `pub mod` declarations when callers need only selected types or functions.
331:

from pathlib import Path
from collections import Counter
files = [
".skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-skilled/references/rust/quick-reference/rustdoc-and-cargo.md",
".skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-skilled/references/rust/style-guide/commenting-and-rustdoc.md",

".skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-skilled/references/rust/style-guide/toolchain-and-project-structure.md",
]
for f in files:
    lines = Path(f).read_text().splitlines()
    sents=[]
    for i,l in enumerate(lines,1):
        if l.startswith(("```","|","-","#","1.","2.","3.","4.","5.","6.","7.","8.","9.","0.")): continue
        for s in re.split(r'(?<=[.!?])\s+', l.strip()):

    c=Counter(s for s,_ in sents)
    dups=[(s,n,[i for ss,i in sents if ss==s]) for s,n in c.items() if n>1]
    print(f.split('/')[-1], dups[:5])
